key_insight: Momentum helps RLVR when its coefficient increases as the learning rate decreases, keeping η/(1−β) in a safe regime so expected gains can dominate sampling fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: RLVR post-training may benefit from tuning momentum jointly with the learning rate rather than retaining a conventional fixed coefficient.
method: Model RLVR as a bandit problem with bias-corrected EMA momentum.
Prove acceleration for exact policy gradients within an overshoot-safe coefficient range.
Analyze sampled-gradient fluctuations and test predictions in bandit simulations and LLM post-training.
evidence_signal: Bandit simulations validate the predictions, Qwen3-4B-Base experiments support larger momentum coefficients, and increasing AdamW β₁ on Qwen2.5-32B improves mean validation accuracy by nearly 2 percentage points over the conventional choice.
watch_item: Larger momentum is not unconditionally better: the theory requires an overshoot-safe regime, and its guarantees are derived in a bandit formulation.
paper_title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
